project.intro: You asked for a way to open a project and get both the big picture and what needs you, working with an agent and paired with Switchboard. Round two adds three things: a walk through Flex's prototype (it has built much of what I proposed), Switchboard's windows (main, project, and a Review window you can tear off), the joys of a Mac app (answering from the menu bar and from notifications, full screen, Spotlight, Quick Look), and Away from the Mac: our Switchboard workflow extended to a Switchboard app on your phone, with ideas from Kazzi and engineering from Fuchi. Start with What Flex built, then Look closer, where the native-or-web question now sits.
project.name: The board: the plan

settled.text: One board per project; Switchboard knows which projects have one.
Every card carries my recommendation and why; obvious calls never get a card; they go on this list, where you can object.
Cards cite their prior art (the context pass), or say plainly there is none.
Dark and light, both real; every action reachable from the keyboard.
The board works from disk with no server, and the copy-to-chat path always works.
Boards, answers and screenshots stay on your Mac and in your repos. Away from the Mac they travel only as sealed rows the store can't read (see Away from the Mac).
PLAN.md, the phase files and WISHLIST.md stay plain files in the repo; the board reads them, it doesn't replace them.
The inbox inside the board stays Needs you.
